title: The Calculation, Thresholds and Reporting of Inter-Limb Strength Asymmetry: A Systematic Review (Parkinson et al. 2021)
content: Parkinson et al. (2021), Journal of Sports Science & Medicine — Inter-limb strength asymmetry, measurement: This systematic review identified twelve distinct methods used in the literature to calculate inter-limb asymmetry, most commonly the Limb Symmetry Index. Only a minority of these indices produce equivalent asymmetry magnitudes regardless of which limb happens to score higher — the authors note that arbitrarily picking a 'reference' limb can bias the result, and recommend normalized indices for consistent reporting.

title: The Calculation, Thresholds and Reporting of Inter-Limb Strength Asymmetry: A Systematic Review (Parkinson et al. 2021)
content: Parkinson et al. (2021) — Asymmetry thresholds: A 10-15% difference between limbs is the threshold most commonly cited in the sports-science literature as 'meaningful' asymmetry (used in 27 of 30 reviewed articles that applied a threshold). However, the review found this specific cutoff has weak evidentiary support — only about a third of studies using it cited strong direct evidence for that number. Healthy, high-performing athletes with no functional deficit can still show asymmetries as high as 13-15%, so a fixed universal threshold does not by itself indicate a problem.

title: The Calculation, Thresholds and Reporting of Inter-Limb Strength Asymmetry: A Systematic Review (Parkinson et al. 2021)
content: Parkinson et al. (2021) — Practical takeaway: The review recommends an individualized approach rather than treating any single asymmetry percentage as a hard rule: use consistent test batteries, consider the person's own typical variability, and interpret a bilateral gap alongside actual performance, pain, or injury history rather than in isolation. Chasing 'perfect' left-right symmetry is not itself a well-supported training goal — some natural asymmetry (e.g. from handedness) is normal.
